To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

heat curing does not have any significant effect on the compressive strength of geopolymer concretes and the addition of polypropylene fibres increases the ductility of the material, and the optimum fibre content is 0.15% (by weight) of the cementitious material.

the compressive strength of geopolymer concretes is not affected by heat curing and that polypropylene fibrous geopolymer concrete has higher strength and ductility compared to conventional fibre-reinforced concrete.
the addition of 0.05 % fibres to geopolymer concrete improves the compressive strength of the concrete and the ductility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of geopolymer cement for the construction industry and the use of synthetic fibres in geopolymers.
investigating the effect of ambient curing and fibre reinforcement on the compressive strength, ductility, and microstructure of geopolymer concretes.
the application of geopolymer concretes in in situ construction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of polypropylene fibre-reinforced ambient cured geopolymer concretes can be a viable alternative to the current construction industry in Australia.
heat curing has a minimal effect on the strength and ductility properties of geopolymer concretes.
geopolymer concrete has a potential to be used in precast members and in situ applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the geopolymer concrete can achieve a compressive strength similar to the conventional concrete with a reduced carbon emission.

geopolymer concrete can be used as an alternative to Portland cement concrete for in situ applications with ambient curing, and that the addition of polypropyle fibres improves the ductility of the material.
the addition of polypropylene fibre in geopolymer concretes is beneficial for both ambient cured and heat-cured concrete samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mechanical performance of geopolymer concretes can be further enhanced by the addition of polypropylene fibres and heat curing.
the mechanical properties of geopolymer can be enhanced with ambient curing and polypropylene fibrous reinforcement.
ambient-cured geopolymer concrete can be used in in situ construction applications.
